title: An Arm That Picks and Places: Inverse Kinematics, Joint Limits, a Timed Cycle, and a Speed Cut by the Distance to a Person

questions.question: Why does arm_pose_for take the elbow up branch for a point sometimes?
options: Elbow up is always tried first
The branch is chosen at random
Elbow up is faster to compute
The elbow down branch may be outside the joint limits, and the other branch fits: there is none only if neither does
questions.explanation: The elbow down branch is preferred. Where the joint limits rule it out, the other branch is used, and the point is refused only if neither fits.

questions.question: What does a tip speed limit of 0.8 m/s cost in cycle time, and what does 0.25 m/s cost?
options: Nothing and nothing: the arm is below both limits
About 4 percent (4.10 to 4.28 s) and about 86 percent (7.63 s)
Half and double the cycle
About 86 percent and about 4 percent
questions.explanation: The arm's tip reaches 1.14 m/s at most, so 0.8 m/s only trims the fastest parts. 0.25 m/s slows nearly all of the loop.

questions.question: At a limit of 0.25 m/s the tip reached 0.30 m/s. Why?
options: The planner has a bug in its limit
The speed was rounded to one decimal
The speed is scaled by a fraction that can only move at a limited rate, so a leg that begins quickly overshoots the limit before the ramp catches up: a target, not a wall
The person moved the limit
questions.explanation: The scaling fraction ramps at a limited rate. A leg that starts fast is over the limit for a moment, so the limit is a target with an overshoot.

questions.question: With somebody 8 cm from the pick point, how close did the monitored arm come, and how many ticks in contact?
options: 0.077 m, and 66 ticks
0.000 m, and 100 ticks
0.150 m, exactly the margin, and 0
0.500 m, and 0 ticks
questions.explanation: The limiter turned the distance into a speed that reached zero at the margin. The arm waited there and finished when the person left.

questions.question: Why does the e-stop stop shorter at the 0.8 m/s limit than at the arm's full speed?
options: The brake is stronger at low speed
The e-stop loop is shorter
The joints are closer to home
The distance to stop grows with the speed it started from (0.044 m against 0.065 m)
questions.explanation: Slowing near people matters twice: for the contact that is avoided, and for the shorter stop when the loop opens.

questions.question: Why is this not what a collaborative arm is certified on?
options: Certification measures contact forces on a test device on the real arm: this models the logic only, with a tip and no inertia
It is certified on its source code
It moves in a plane only
It has no gripper
questions.explanation: Certification is about the force and pressure of a real contact, measured on the real arm. This model has a tip, a speed and no inertia.
